title: macOS Tahoe — Full Desktop
originalPrompt: Recreate the whole MacOs tahoe interface as a web app. Every app and menu should be working

questionsAndAnswers.question: What web stack should I use? I'm assuming React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind CSS for a modern component-based recreation unless you prefer something else.
macOS Tahoe includes many apps and menus. Which core components must be included in the first version? 'Every app' is huge, so I recommend starting with the shell + a few canonical apps.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Desktop, Dock, and top Menu Bar; Finder (file manager with folders, files, icons, sidebar); System Settings / Control Center; Safari browser (basic web view or mocked pages); Terminal; Calculator and Notes; Literally every default macOS app (Mail, Messages, Maps, Calendar, Photos, Music, TV, etc.); Window manager (drag, resize, minimize, maximize, fullscreen)

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does 'every app and menu should be working' mean to you?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Visually faithful and interactively functional within the simulated OS (no real backend / accounts)

questionsAndAnswers.question: Should I deliver this in phases (Desktop/Dock/Menu Bar + Finder first, then additional apps), or do you want all apps built together in one block? I strongly recommend phased delivery so each layer can be verified.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Phased: shell and core apps first, then remaining apps in groups

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should simulated data (files, folders, notes, settings) persist across reloads?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No persistence: fresh demo state on every reload

questionsAndAnswers.question: What browsers/devices should this support?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Modern Chrome, Safari, Edge desktop only

questionsAndAnswers.question: What automated testing do you want? Visual fidelity is hard to unit-test, so I recommend unit tests for state/logic plus manual QA checklists for UI behavior.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Unit tests for state/logic + manual QA checklist for UI behavior

questionsAndAnswers.question: Where should this be deployable?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No specific deployment target; local dev only

title: macOS Tahoe — Core Shell

questionsAndAnswers.question: What level of functional depth are you aiming for?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Interactive UI shell: menus launch apps, windows open/drag/resize, but most app contents are simulated/stubbed

questionsAndAnswers.question: Do you have a preferred technology stack?
Which bundled macOS apps and system areas are must-haves vs. can be stubbed/skipped?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Finder (file manager); Dock; Menu Bar (global menu); Control Center / System Settings; Spotlight / Search; Basic apps (Calculator, Notes, Calendar, Clock, Safari shell)

questionsAndAnswers.question: macOS Tahoe is not yet released. What visual reference should drive the design?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Use publicly available Tahoe leaks/announcements and extrapolate from current macOS design language

questionsAndAnswers.question: Should window positions, open apps, and user-created data (e.g., Notes) persist across page reloads?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No, start fresh on every reload
